final:
A lost, exhausted girl took shelter in what was genuinely an empty house and lay down to rest. All through the night she was kept awake by fear: a figure was at the window, looking in and watching her as she tried to sleep. She could have recognized the truth earlier, since it was there and plainly visible the whole time, but in the dark she took it at face value—a person outside, staring in. Finally, worn out, she fell asleep.

When she woke in the morning the figure was gone, and daylight showed her what the window truly was and what she had actually been seeing. The "watcher" had never been a real intruder outside the glass; the dark pane had been acting as a mirror, throwing back an image from within, so that what terrified her all night was a reflection rather than a person in the yard. Understanding that the thing she had feared and stared at through the long night was an illusion—and what that implied about the room around her—she panicked and fled the house in terror.
